elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Rendered 15.6 retains the proviso, now limited to us: "provided, however, that PB may assign, sublicense or transfer this Agreement and all of its rights and obligations hereunder, in their entirety, to any of its Affiliates" — an express no-consent affiliate transfer for PB (Customer).

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Same proviso continues: "or to a successor in connection with the sale or other transfer of all or substantially all of its business or assets to which this Agreement relates, whether by merger, sale of stock, sale of assets or otherwise" — merger, stock sale and substantially-all-assets successors are all covered without consent.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: By narrowing the proviso from "either Party" to "PB", SFJ is left inside the general bar: "Without the prior written consent of the other Party hereto ... neither Party will sell, transfer, assign, pledge or otherwise dispose of ... this Agreement or any of its rights or duties hereunder." SFJ therefore has no remaining no-consent exception.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Inserted into the operative consent requirement: "Without the prior written consent of the other Party hereto, not to be unreasonably withheld". The competitor sentence's "sole discretion" standard is expressly framed as "Notwithstanding any of the foregoing", so it carves out rather than contradicts.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: Retained and extended: "SFJ shall not sell, assign, sublicense or otherwise transfer this Agreement to an entity whose primary business is the development or commercialization of pharmaceutical or biotechnology products at any time", with the Program Transfer sunset and the confirming "For the avoidance of doubt" sentence deleted. The only relaxation is PB's own sole-discretion consent, which is a Customer waiver, not a Vendor right.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: 14.2.6 as rendered states: "SFJ shall have no right to terminate this Agreement as a result of a Change of Control of PB." The prior sole-discretion termination right and the 150% Development Costs payment that was payable only "[i]n the event that SFJ terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 14.2.6" are gone; the heading is conformed to "Change of Control of PB".

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: The proviso was deliberately narrowed to "PB may assign ... to a successor"; SFJ now needs prior written consent for any transfer, so the fallback's mutual successor right is absent (an intentional trade-off, since the preferred level is reached).

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: No notice mechanic attaches to a 15.6 successor transfer; the only notice retained is PB's Change-of-Control notice in 14.2.6, which is not an assignment-notice covenant.
PB retains a no-consent affiliate exception ("to any of its Affiliates"), a non-successor exception which under the fallback checklist defeats the requirement that all other assignments need consent.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "Without the prior written consent of the other Party hereto, not to be unreasonably withheld" supplies the reasonableness standard for all consent-gated transfers.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all six preferred elements are met in operative language (affiliate and successor carve-outs retained for PB only; SFJ assignment consent-gated with a reasonableness standard; permanent competitor bar; express no-termination-on-Change-of-Control statement).

Fallback is not met (no mutual successor right, no written-notice mechanic, and a retained PB affiliate exception), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is complete; declining the fallback is correct since it would surrender our own consent-free affiliate carve-out.

Minimality holds. Each edit maps to a preferred element: (i) "not to be unreasonably withheld" for the consent standard; (ii) "either Party" to "PB" to close SFJ's self-help exception; (iii) deleting the Program Transfer sunset and its avoidance-of-doubt sentence, which directly contradicts the "at any time" competitor bar; (iv) replacing the 14.2.6 termination right. No survival tails, expense language, extra remedies or unrelated boilerplate were added, and favourable existing wording (the full merger/stock/asset successor list, PB's sole-discretion consent over competitor transfers) is preserved.

Deleting the 150% Development Costs payment and the p0766 consequences is repair, not surplus: both were expressly conditioned on "the event that SFJ terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 14.2.6" and on "the date of such termination", so retaining them would leave contradictory, inoperative text keyed to a removed right. PB's Article 6 Approval Payment obligations and the 6.7.2 Buy-Out Option are independent and survive untouched.

Intent preserved: PB's Change-of-Control notification covenant to SFJ is retained, the Trial Data Package / Section 11.1.1.4 purchase mechanic is untouched outside the deleted termination scenario, and SFJ's limited-partner/liquidating-trust right to assign receipt of Approval Payments is left in place.

Residual point to confirm rather than a defect: the drafter asserts no other provision cross-references Section 14.2.6. Before sending, run a document-wide check for "14.2.6" (including Article 11 and any termination-consequences schedule) so the deletion leaves no dangling cross-reference.

Optional polish only, not a gating defect: the successor carve-out is qualified by "business or assets to which this Agreement relates"; that language is pre-existing and favourable enough to leave alone, and the margin comment already explains the change concisely and offers the correct rationale.
